geometry_edits.rationale: Increase section articulation while preserving one coherent primary mass.
Moderate the stepbacks to keep the mass continuous and capacity-bearing.
Expand the carved public void so the frontage response reads clearly in plan and elevation.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the stepped upper hierarchy while keeping a single continuous dominant mass.
Slightly reduce the stairiness so the silhouette reads as a more continuous inhabited section.
Open the public threshold a bit more so the access-side void is more legible at ground level.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent stepped neighborhood mass in all four views, with a single dominant volume and a carved public void that gives the ground plane some legibility. The parcel containment appears coherent and the mass responds to the site frame rather than merely filling a box. The blue frontage edge is answered by an access seam/void rather than a sealed face, which supports the neighborhood-living brief. The main weakness is that the section is still somewhat generic and stair-like, but the silhouette remains capacity-bearing enough to pass for an early massing study. It is also compatible with the reference set: especially the courtyard/threshold logic in the similar neighborhood community precedents.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and enclosed than the candidate; do not copy the curved parapet language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a central void and layered upper volumes can create a civic neighborhood threshold without becoming a pure box.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a larger multi-building complex; candidate should stay compact and not fragment into separate blocks.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, courtyard-centered composition supports a campus-like neighborhood program and can absorb multiple masses around a common public realm.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more rectilinear and polished; candidate should keep its own stepped profile.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear central cut or recessed court with an overhanging upper mass gives a legible public ground response and active edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Avoid over-extending the plan; the candidate is more compact and should not become a long bar.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise massing with a courtyard and gentle roof slope can support mixed neighborhood use while staying horizontal.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more distributed and landscape-heavy; candidate should keep a single dominant mass and not over-split.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Bridging, terracing, and multi-wing organization around open space can preserve hierarchy while enriching public circulation.
